C21 supplies a similar correspondence format with Adenauer but concerns unrelated economic claims, while C20 shares Geneva and divided-country themes without the same German reunification/Western-unity argument.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I consider that the reunification of your country is of first importance in the process of establishing foundations for a lasting peace.","parent_excerpt":"there can be no solution without free elections and the formation of a free all-German government, leading to unification... culminating in an honorable peace treaty and the re-emergence of a new united German Republic","explanation":"Both make German reunification a central step in establishing peace, using closely parallel policy logic."},{"child_excerpt":"the maintenance of Western unity is vital to the ultimate achievement of these objectives","parent_excerpt":"the strengthening of the Federal Republic... and further progress in the integration of Western Europe, can only enhance the prospects for the peaceful unification of Germany","explanation":"The child restates C10's machinery of using Western cohesion and integration to advance peaceful German reunification."},{"child_excerpt":"We must now look forward to a period of arduous and continuing negotiation in the effort to achieve the aims of peace and justice","parent_excerpt":"the peace we all so dearly seek cannot be maintained through weakness... strength for peace","explanation":"Both frame continuing Western policy toward Germany as a coordinated effort to achieve peace, though the child's wording is substantially condensed."}]}
